Your yard, drawn before it is built

We draw your yard on paper first: where the patio sits, where the water goes, what gets planted. Then a crew builds from that drawing.

Sheet L-1Services

Six jobs, one drawing

Many yards need more than one of these. We scope them together so the drainage under the patio and the lights over it are decided before anyone digs.

Areas served (placeholders): Charlotte, Matthews, Huntersville, Mint Hill, Pineville.

  • Patios and walkways

    Pavers, flagstone and poured surfaces, laid on a compacted base, the step that matters most for a flat surface. Edges, steps and seating walls are part of the same drawing.

    CostPriced by material, area and base depth.
  • Retaining walls and steps

    Stone or block walls that hold a slope, with drainage behind them. Taller walls may need an engineer's drawing and a permit, which we flag early.

    CostPriced by wall height, length and stone.
  • Planting design

    Beds laid out for sun, soil and mature size, with a plant list you can read. Native and low-water choices where they fit.

    CostPriced by bed size and plant sizes.
  • Outdoor lighting

    Low-voltage path, step and accent lights on a transformer with a timer. Placed in the evening, when you can see what they do.

    CostPriced by fixture count and wire runs.
  • Drainage and grading

    Swales, downspout lines, buried drain pipe, catch basins and regrading for yards that hold water. Often the first thing to fix, and the least visible when done.

    CostPriced by slope, soil and pipe length.
  • Lawn care and seasonal upkeep

    Mowing, aeration, overseeding, pruning and mulch on a schedule that follows the season, for new and existing yards.

    CostPriced by lawn size and visit frequency.

Sheet L-4Process

Five phases, in the order they happen

Each phase ends with something on paper you can read and change before the next one starts.

  1. Walk the site

    We measure, note sun, slope and where water goes, and mark anything underground. The 811 utility locate is requested before any digging.

  2. Draft the plan

    A drawing of the layout and a planting list, so you can see the patio, beds and paths before they exist.

  3. Review and adjust

    A written scope with materials and a schedule. You change what you want changed. HOA and permit steps are flagged here.

  4. Build and hand over

    The crew builds from the drawing, cleans up, and leaves a care sheet for new plants and surfaces.

  5. Keep it up

    Optional seasonal visits for mowing, aeration, pruning and mulch, on a written schedule.

Permits, inspections and engineering

We tell you which apply to your yard in the written scope, before work starts. They most often come up for:

  • Retaining walls over a set height
  • Drainage changes
  • Some outdoor structures

Sheet L-6General notes

Landscaping questions, answered

How is a project priced?

By scope. Square footage, materials, access and site conditions all move the number, so the price comes after we see the yard and write the scope. You approve the written scope before work begins.

Do I need a plan before I hire anyone?

No. Drafting the plan is part of how we work. If you already have a drawing from an architect or a previous contractor, bring it and we will build from it or suggest changes.

What about permits and my HOA?

Some work needs them and some does not. Taller retaining walls, drainage changes and structures often do. We tell you which apply in the written scope, and we can help prepare the drawings an HOA asks for.

How long does a patio take?

It depends on size, material, weather and base preparation. We give a schedule in the written scope, and we tell you if rain or a material delay moves it.

What does lawn care include, and how often?

Mowing, edging and cleanup on a regular cycle, plus seasonal work such as aeration, overseeding, pruning and mulch. How often depends on grass type, lawn size and the time of year. The schedule is written down.

Can you work around plants and trees I want to keep?

Yes. We mark what stays on the plan and protect those roots during the build. If a tree is in the way of a layout, we show the options and you choose.

What a first visit covers

A short walk of the yard with you. Nothing to prepare beyond what you want to change.

  • We note sun, slope and where water goes
  • We measure the areas you care about
  • We ask what you want to do outside, and what to keep
  • You get a written scope to read before deciding
